the results of the study are not sufficient to draw any firm conclusions regarding the effects of social support on the exosomal profile in ovarian cancer patients.
the exosome transcriptomic profile is modulated by the social environment of the patient and that this is associated with EMT polarization, inflammation and β‐ adrenergic signaling in ovarian cancer.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
social factors in the patient microenvironment are associated with changes in exosomal profiles that are related to EMT, inflammation, and β‐adrenoceptor signaling.
the biobehaviorally modulated exosomes are associated with the EMT phenotype, inflammation, and the sympathetic nervous system.
the exosome transcriptomic profile is sensitive to the biobehaviorally‐induced polarization of the tumor microenvironment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social support can be measured by the exosomal profile of ovarian cancer.
social support is a modifiable factor with the potential to impact tumor biology and patient outcomes.
exosomes are a potential tool for monitoring the effects of biobearhavioral factors on cancer biology over time and for understanding the role of social factors in cancer biology.
